posts.name: silopolis
posts.cooked:
We like to set up games that "make sense." Then when we inevitably lose, we reroll the game with our "heavy hitters", a small group of characters that we seem to do really well with.

We did do Miss Information vs. Freedom Five (well, four of them) in Freedom Tower, and we did do the Jan Brady game (Omnitron, Omnitron, Omnitron!), and we did F4 vs. V4 (all F5ers minus AZ, all V5ers minus Prole). We did Chrono Ranger, Omni-X, Visionary, and KNYFE vs. La Capitan in Silver Gulch for a little time-travel shenanigans. We did Ra + three others vs. the Ennead in the Tomb of Anubis.

I have a hard time doing games that seem completely random. the Chairman in the Enclave of the Endlings, or Spite in the Doktorath Capital. There's just a little mental block there. I have to see the story and be able to say, "Oh, Spite's attacking the Block to get at some drugs they have in the infirmary" for the game to make sense to me. I have bent that rule only for games against villains we NEED to defeat for catharsis purposes... La Capitan, Matriarch, and the Chairman have all attacked the Mobile Defense Platform, much to the chagrin of Baron Blade's various Mechanics and Shield Generators, who basically seem to sit there and hang out with themselves while our battle rages on. ;) Villains used to attack Freedom Tower with some regularity, as well, until there came too many Forced Entries and the Simulation Room kept acting up. Now Our Heroes tend to try to take those fights elsewhere. ;)
